# Summary of the BNP 2010 Manifesto

The British National Party's 2010 manifesto presents a comprehensive vision centered on preserving Britain's indigenous population, culture, and sovereignty against what it identifies as existential threats from mass immigration, Islamic colonisation, and European Union membership.

## Core Ideology

The manifesto frames the indigenous British people—English, Scots, Welsh, and Irish—as facing demographic extinction within decades due to immigration and differential birth rates. It asserts that multicultural societies inevitably fracture and collapse, citing Rome and Rwanda as examples, and argues that group identity and nationhood are expressions of innate genetic nature.

## Immigration Policy

The BNP proposes halting all further immigration, deporting illegal immigrants and foreign criminals, ending the "asylum swindle," and promoting voluntary repatriation with financial incentives. It pledges to review all citizenship grants since 1997, arguing Labour deliberately engineered mass immigration to "change forcibly Britain's demographics." The party would repeal the Race Relations Act and abolish all "politically correct" social engineering projects.

## Counter-Jihad

The manifesto identifies Islam as fundamentally incompatible with Western democracy, citing historical conflicts and demographic projections showing Muslim population growth. It proposes banning burkas, ritual slaughter, and mosque construction, halting all Muslim immigration, and deporting radical preachers. The party claims Islamist terrorism stems from mass immigration combined with biased British foreign policy favouring Israel.

## European Union

The BNP demands immediate EU withdrawal, arguing the organisation usurps British sovereignty and imposes costly regulations. It claims 80% of British laws originate from Brussels and membership costs billions annually.

## Economic Vision

The manifesto proposes cutting foreign aid (£9.1 billion), EU membership fees (£15 billion), climate change programmes (£18 billion), and immigration-related costs (£13 billion). These savings would fund the NHS, pensions, and industrial regeneration. It advocates protectionism, tariffs on Third World imports, and rebuilding British manufacturing through investment in engineering and science education.

## Social Policies

The BNP would "renationalise the welfare state," restricting benefits to British citizens who have contributed. It proposes grammar schools, traditional teaching methods, capital punishment for certain crimes, and a community service scheme for school leavers. The party pledges to restore civil liberties eroded under "anti-terror" legislation while repealing the Human Rights Act.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

British troops would be withdrawn from Afghanistan, and the party opposes war with Iran. It advocates military independence from NATO and neutrality in Middle Eastern affairs, proposing a "peace treaty" with the Islamic world involving non-interference in exchange for halting Islamic immigration to Britain.
